I just learned that this configuration must no longer be used. I do not know why though.
The new way of achieving this would be to disable automatic pulling and pull using an automation as stated here:

Just deactivate the option for automatic polling under the integrations "System options" and create an automation, which handles polling instead.

Unfortunately the requested change was rejected, so there won't be another solution for this, but to use automations. HA Core Dev Team decided that changing the refresh interval must not be used anymore.

I am also no big fan of using automations when there is another way, but we can't do anything about it.

We aim to provide a sane scan interval out of the box by default for all integrations.

A refresh/scan interval option for integrations in the UI sounds natural (and thus, we did in the past). However, we learned it is not. For example:

Some people really don't know the impact of these and just set them to the lowest they can, like 1 second. Leading to weird behaviors, and above all, more often, some API providers become victims of this, processing so many requests that they end up blocking Home Assistant (in which case everybody loses).

Another trend: Lots of specialized feature requests/configuration options for customization scan intervals became a thing. E.g., to poll less on paid APIs when away from home, not polling battery-powered devices during the night, and tons of other variants like these.

To keep the experience unified and to maximize the possibilities of polling in any way one would like, we have made a service for this, allowing for automation to do anything in any way you like, in any schedule, taking any condition you like into account. We agree that isn't always easy, but considering the first point, that isn't the goal.

Glances implements this correctly to our standards now, so I'm going to close this issue.

./Frenck
